name: Barbell Back Squat
description: A compound lower-body lift that builds the quads, glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Set the bar on a rack at upper-chest height and step under it so it rests across your upper back, not your neck.
Unrack the bar, step back and set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes slightly turned out.
Brace your core and take a deep breath before you start down.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Keep your chest up and your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your whole foot to stand up, exhaling as you rise.
tips: Set the rack safety pins just below your lowest squat depth.
Start light to learn the movement before adding weight.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom.

name: Conventional Deadlift
description: A full-body pull from the floor that builds the hamstrings, glutes and back.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Hinge at the hips and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Flatten your back, lift your chest and brace your core.
Push the floor away with your legs, keeping the bar close to your body.
Stand tall at the top by locking out your hips and knees and squeezing your glutes.
Lower the bar by hinging your hips back first, then bending your knees, keeping the bar close.
tips: Keep the bar touching your legs all the way up.
Reset your brace on every rep.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift away from your body.
Jerking the bar off the floor.

name: Barbell Bench Press
description: A classic horizontal press for the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and pull your shoulder blades together.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with straight arms.
Lower the bar to your mid-chest under control, with elbows about 45 to 60 degrees from your torso.
Press the bar up until your arms are straight.
tips: Use a spotter or safety arms when lifting heavy.
Keep your feet planted and your glutes on the bench.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees.
Lifting the hips off the bench.

name: Barbell Overhead Press
description: A standing press that builds the shoulders and triceps.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and the bar at collarbone height, hands just outside your shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head slightly back so the bar passes your face.
Lock out overhead with the bar above the middle of your feet.
Lower the bar back to your collarbone under control.
tips: Squeeze your glutes to protect your lower back.
commonMistakes: Pressing the bar out in front instead of straight up.
Using your legs to jerk the bar up.

name: Pull-Up
description: A bodyweight pull that builds the lats, upper back and biceps.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Pull your shoulder blades down to start the movement.
Pull your chest toward the bar, driving your elbows down.
Get your chin above the bar.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.
tips: Use a resistance band or assisted machine if you cannot do a full rep yet.
Avoid swinging.
commonMistakes: Not lowering to a full hang.
Shrugging your shoulders toward your ears.

name: Push-Up
description: A bodyweight press for the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Brace your abs and glutes.
Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Stop just above the floor.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Drop to your knees or put your hands on a bench to make it easier.

name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
description: A walking lunge that builds the quads and glutes and trains balance.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand tall.
Step forward with one leg.
Lower your back knee toward the floor until both knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and your torso upright.
Push through your front heel and step the back foot forward into the next lunge.
Alternate legs as you walk forward.
tips: Take steps long enough that your front knee stays over your ankle.
Keep your chest up throughout.
commonMistakes: Steps that are too short, which overloads the front knee.
Letting the front knee cave inward.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
description: An isolation exercise for the biceps.
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and elbows by your sides.
Curl the weights toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower the weights slowly until your arms are fully straight.
tips: Lower the weight for 2 to 3 seconds to get more from each rep.

name: Triceps Rope Pushdown
description: A cable isolation exercise for the triceps.
steps: Attach a rope to a high pulley and grip it with your palms facing each other.
Tuck your elbows against your sides.
Push the rope down until your arms are straight, spreading the ends apart at the bottom.
Squeeze your triceps.
Let the rope rise slowly until your forearms are just past 90 degrees.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
commonMistakes: Letting your shoulders do the pushing.

name: Lat Pulldown
description: A cable pull that builds the lats and upper back.
steps: Sit with your thighs secured under the pads and grip the bar with an overhand grip wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest.
Pull the bar to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are fully extended.
tips: Think about pulling with your elbows, not your hands.
commonMistakes: Pulling the bar behind your neck.
Leaning back too far and swinging.

name: Plank
description: An isometric hold that trains the core.
steps: Place your forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders.
Extend your legs with your toes on the floor.
Make a straight line from your head to your heels.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe steadily and hold.
tips: End the set when your hips start to sag. Good form matters more than time.
commonMistakes: Hips sagging or rising too high.
Looking forward and straining your neck.

name: Burpee
description: A full-body conditioning move that raises your heart rate fast.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Jump or step your feet back into a high plank.
Lower your chest to the floor or do a push-up.
Jump or step your feet back toward your hands.
Jump up with your arms overhead.
tips: Step back instead of jumping to reduce impact.

name: Jump Rope
description: A simple, high-intensity cardio exercise that also trains coordination.
steps: Hold the handles at hip height with your elbows close to your sides.
Swing the rope overhead using your wrists, not your whole arms.
Jump just high enough to clear the rope, about 2 to 3 centimeters.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Keep a steady rhythm.
tips: Pick a rope that reaches your armpits when you stand on its middle.
commonMistakes: Swinging the rope from the shoulders.

name: Treadmill Running
description: Steady-state running on a treadmill for cardio fitness.
steps: Clip the safety key to your clothing and stand on the side rails.
Start the belt at a slow walk and step on.
Increase the speed gradually to a comfortable jog.
Land softly with your feet under your body, with relaxed shoulders and arms bent about 90 degrees.
Look ahead, not down at the belt.
Finish with 3 to 5 minutes of walking to cool down.
tips: Set the incline to 1 percent to better match outdoor running.

name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
description: A gentle stretch for the back of the thigh.
steps: Sit on the floor with one leg straight and the other foot against your inner thigh.
Hinge forward from your hips, keeping your back long.
Reach toward your foot until you feel a stretch behind your thigh.
Hold while breathing slowly, then switch legs.
tips: Stretch to mild tension, never pain.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach farther.

name: Jumping Jacks
description: A classic full-body cardio move that warms you up and raises your heart rate.
steps: Stand tall with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
Jump your feet out wide while swinging your arms overhead.
Jump back to the start position with your feet together and your arms down.
Keep a steady rhythm and breathe evenly.
tips: Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Step side to side instead of jumping to lower the impact.

name: High Knees
description: Running in place with your knees driven high, a quick way to build cardio fitness.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up toward hip height, then switch quickly to the other leg.
Pump your arms in rhythm with your legs.
Stay on the balls of your feet and keep your chest up.
tips: Slow to a march if you need to reduce the impact.
Keep your core braced.
commonMistakes: Knees that only rise a little.

name: Butt Kicks
description: A running drill that kicks the heels toward the glutes to warm up the hamstrings.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Jog in place and kick your heels up toward your glutes.
Keep your thighs mostly pointing down and your torso upright.
Swing your arms naturally.
tips: Stay light on the balls of your feet.
Start slowly and build speed.
commonMistakes: Lifting the knees instead of the heels.

name: Mountain Climber
description: A plank-based cardio move that drives your knees to your chest and works the core.
steps: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Switch legs quickly, as if running in place.
Keep your hips level and your core tight.
tips: Slow the pace to focus on form.
Keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists.

name: Jump Squat
description: An explosive squat that builds leg power and raises your heart rate.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower into a squat by pushing your hips back.
Drive through your feet and jump straight up.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and go straight into the next squat.
tips: Land with bent knees to absorb the impact.
Do a regular squat instead if jumping hurts your knees.

name: Bodyweight Squat
description: A basic squat that builds the legs and glutes with no equipment.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes slightly turned out.
Push your hips back and bend your knees.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
tips: Reach your arms forward to help your balance.
Keep your weight on your heels and mid-foot.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: A step-back lunge that is easier on the knees than a forward lunge.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and your torso upright.
Push through your front foot to return to standing, then switch legs.
tips: Hold a wall or chair for balance at first.
Take a big enough step back to keep your front shin vertical.
commonMistakes: Front knee drifting past your toes.

name: Glute Bridge
description: A floor exercise that targets the glutes and the back of the legs.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Brace your core and press through your heels.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
tips: Pause for a second at the top to feel the squeeze.
Keep your ribs down.

name: Wall Sit
description: An isometric hold that burns the quads without any equipment.
steps: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet about 60 cm in front of you.
Slide down until your knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Keep your back flat against the wall and your knees over your ankles.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
tips: Rest your hands on your thighs, not on your knees.
Build up the hold time gradually.

name: Calf Raise
description: A simple lift that builds the calf muscles.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, near a wall for balance if you need it.
Press through the balls of your feet and rise as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your heels slowly back to the floor.
tips: Lower for 2 to 3 seconds on each rep.
Do it on a step for a bigger range of motion.

name: Knee Push-Up
description: An easier push-up from the knees that builds the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Walk your knees back so your body forms a straight line from your head to your knees.
Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Cross your ankles to stay stable.
Progress to full push-ups when you can do 15 clean reps.

name: Diamond Push-Up
description: A close-grip push-up that puts extra work on the triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank with your hands together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond.
Keep your body in a straight line and brace your core.
Lower your chest toward your hands with your elbows close to your body.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Drop to your knees to make it easier.
Keep your elbows tucked.

name: Pike Push-Up
description: An inverted push-up that targets the shoulders.
steps: Start in a high plank, then walk your feet in and lift your hips high so your body forms an upside-down V.
Keep your arms and legs as straight as you can.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor.
Push back up to the starting position.
tips: Keep your head between your arms, not in front of them.
Move your feet closer to your hands to make it harder.

name: Superman
description: A back extension that strengthens the lower back and glutes.
steps: Lie face down with your arms extended in front of you and your legs straight.
Lift your arms, chest and legs a few centimeters off the floor at the same time.
Squeeze your glutes and lower back for a second at the top.
Lower back down slowly.
tips: Keep your neck in line with your spine.
Move slowly, without jerking.

name: Crunch
description: A basic ab exercise that works the upper abs.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest.
Curl your shoulders off the floor by tightening your abs.
Lower back down with control.
tips: Look at the ceiling to keep your neck relaxed.
Exhale as you curl up.
commonMistakes: Lifting the lower back off the floor.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: A rotating ab exercise that works the abs and obliques.
steps: Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head and your legs lifted.
Bring one knee toward your chest while rotating the opposite elbow toward it.
Extend that leg and switch sides in a pedalling motion.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
tips: Rotate from your torso, not just your elbows.
Slow down to feel the abs working.

name: Leg Raise
description: A lying leg lift that targets the lower abs.
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your hands by your sides or under your hips.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Raise your legs until they point straight up.
Lower them slowly without letting your back arch.
tips: Bend your knees slightly to make it easier.
Stop the lowering before your back lifts off the floor.

name: Russian Twist
description: A seated rotation that works the obliques.
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and lean back slightly, keeping your back straight.
Lift your feet off the floor or keep them down to make it easier.
Clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso to one side, then the other.
tips: Keep your chest up and your spine long.
Hold a light weight to make it harder.

name: Side Plank
description: A side hold that builds the obliques and the stabilizing muscles around the hips.
steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and your legs stacked.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Brace your core and breathe steadily.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Bend your bottom knee to make it easier.
Keep your hips from sinking.
commonMistakes: Rolling the body forward or back.

name: Cobra Stretch
description: A gentle back-bend that stretches the abs and chest.
steps: Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders.
Press through your hands and slowly lift your chest off the floor.
Keep your hips on the floor and your shoulders relaxed away from your ears.
Hold while breathing slowly, then lower down.
tips: Only go as high as feels comfortable.
Keep your neck long.
commonMistakes: Pushing into pain in the lower back.

name: Arm Circles
description: Loosens the shoulder joints before any pressing or pulling.
steps: Stand tall with your arms straight out to the sides.
Make small circles, slowly getting bigger.
Do 15 seconds forward, then 15 seconds backward.
tips: Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Breathe normally.

name: Leg Swings
description: Opens up the hips and hamstrings for squats, lunges and deadlifts.
steps: Hold a wall or rack for balance.
Swing one leg forward and back in a controlled arc.
Do 10 swings, then switch legs. Repeat side to side if you like.
tips: Stand tall and keep your core tight.
Let the swing get bigger gradually.
commonMistakes: Leaning the torso to swing higher.
Kicking hard instead of swinging smoothly.

name: Bodyweight Squat (Warm-up)
description: Wakes up the legs and hips and grooves the squat pattern.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Sit your hips back and down as far as is comfortable.
Drive through your feet to stand. Do 10 slow reps.
tips: Keep your chest up and heels down.
Push your knees out in line with your toes.

name: Cat-Cow
description: Mobilises the spine and gets the lower back moving.
steps: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Breathe in, drop your belly and lift your head and tailbone (cow).
Breathe out, round your back and tuck your chin (cat). Repeat for 10 slow breaths.
tips: Move with your breath.
Go through the full range slowly.
commonMistakes: Only moving the neck instead of the whole spine.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
description: A full-body mobility move covering hips, hamstrings, back and shoulders.
steps: Step into a deep lunge with your right foot forward.
Place your left hand on the floor and rotate your right arm up to the ceiling.
Hold for a breath, then switch sides. Do 5 per side.
tips: Keep the back leg straight and strong.
Follow your raised hand with your eyes.
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee collapse inward.

name: Thoracic Rotations
description: Frees up the upper back so you can brace and press or row with good form.
steps: Start on all fours with one hand behind your head.
Rotate that elbow down toward the opposite wrist, then open up toward the ceiling.
Do 8 reps, then switch sides.
tips: Rotate from the upper back, not the lower back.
Keep your hips square.
commonMistakes: Swinging the arm instead of rotating the spine.

name: Goblet Squat
description: A dumbbell squat held at the chest that builds the quads and glutes and teaches good squat form.
steps: Hold one dumbbell upright against your chest with both hands cupped under the top end.
Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and your toes turned out a little.
Brace your core, then sit your hips down and back between your knees.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and your elbows inside your knees.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
tips: Keep the dumbbell pressed against your chest the whole set.
Pick a weight you can hold comfortably before going heavier.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward and letting the dumbbell drift away from your chest.

name: Leg Press
description: A machine press that builds the quads and glutes with the back fully supported.
steps: Sit with your back and hips flat against the pad and place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety handles and hold the side grips.
Lower the platform by bending your knees until they are about 90 degrees.
Keep your lower back on the pad and your knees in line with your toes.
Press through your whole foot until your legs are almost straight, then reset the safeties when you finish.
tips: Stop just short of locking your knees.
Start light until you learn the foot position.
commonMistakes: Lower back rounding off the pad.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: A balance-based hip hinge that builds the hamstrings and glutes with no equipment.
steps: Stand on one leg with a soft bend in the knee and your other foot just off the floor.
Hinge at your hips, pushing them back while your free leg extends straight behind you.
Lower your torso toward parallel with the floor, keeping your back flat and your arms hanging down.
Squeeze your glute to return upright.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.
tips: Rest one hand on a wall or chair for balance at first.
Fix your eyes on a spot on the floor a short way ahead.
commonMistakes: Opening the hips out to the side.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
description: A dumbbell hip hinge that builds the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Soften your knees and push your hips back, sliding the dumbbells down your legs.
Keep your back flat and lower until you feel a stretch behind your thighs, around mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top.
tips: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs the whole way.
Think of pushing your hips back, not bending down.

name: Hip Thrust
description: A barbell lift that targets the glutes harder than a bodyweight bridge.
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a padded barbell over your hips.
Plant your feet flat, hip-width apart, with your knees bent.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips.
Stop when your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees and squeeze your glutes.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.
tips: Use a bar pad to protect your hips.
Keep your chin tucked and your ribs down.
commonMistakes: Over-arching the lower back at the top.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: A dumbbell press for the chest, shoulders and triceps with a freer range than a barbell.
steps: Sit on a bench with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to your chest.
Plant your feet flat and pull your shoulder blades together.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight over your chest.
Lower them under control with your elbows about 45 to 60 degrees from your torso until they reach chest level.
Press back up.
tips: Pick a weight you can control through the full range.
Keep your feet planted and your glutes on the bench.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees.
Bouncing the weights off your chest.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: An overhead dumbbell press that builds the shoulders and triceps.
steps: Sit or stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward.
Brace your core.
Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are straight.
Lower them back to about ear level under control.
tips: Squeeze your glutes if you are standing.
Sit with back support when the weights get heavy.
commonMistakes: Pressing the weights out in front of you.

name: Inverted Row
description: A bodyweight row that builds the upper back and biceps using a low bar or a sturdy table.
steps: Set a bar at about waist height, or use the edge of a sturdy table, and lie underneath it.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder-width with your arms straight and your heels on the floor.
Keep your body in a straight line and pull your chest toward the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself slowly back to straight arms.
tips: Bend your knees to make it easier, or walk your feet forward to make it harder.
Only use a table that is heavy and will not slide or tip.

name: Band Row
description: A resistance-band row that builds the upper back and works at home with no weights.
steps: Anchor a band around a sturdy post at chest height, or sit on the floor with the band looped around your feet.
Hold the ends with your arms straight and your back tall.
Pull the handles toward your ribs, driving your elbows past your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly to straight arms.
tips: Step back or choose a thicker band to make it harder.
Keep your ribs down and your chest tall.

name: Dumbbell Row
description: A one-arm row that builds the lats and upper back.
steps: Place one hand and the same-side knee on a bench with your other foot on the floor and your back flat.
Hold a dumbbell in your free hand with your arm hanging straight down.
Pull your elbow toward your hip, squeezing your back at the top.
Lower the dumbbell slowly to a full stretch.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your hips and shoulders square to the floor.
Think of pulling with your elbow, not your hand.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: A cable row that builds the upper back with the torso supported.
steps: Sit at a row station with your feet on the platform and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the handle and sit tall with your arms straight.
Pull the handle to your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Let the handle return slowly without rounding your back.
tips: Keep your torso still instead of rocking.
Pause for a second at the end of each pull.

name: Bench Dip
description: A bodyweight dip off a bench or chair that builds the triceps.
steps: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench or chair with your hands beside your hips gripping the edge.
Slide your hips off the edge with your knees bent and your feet flat.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until they are about 90 degrees, keeping your back close to the bench.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Straighten your legs to make it harder.
commonMistakes: Hips drifting far from the bench.
Lowering too deep and straining the shoulders.

name: Hammer Curl
description: A neutral-grip curl that builds the biceps and forearms.
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your elbows by your sides.
Curl the weights toward your shoulders, keeping your palms facing in.
Squeeze at the top without moving your upper arms.
Lower the weights slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Lower for 2 to 3 seconds on each rep.
Keep your wrists straight.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension
description: An overhead dumbbell extension that isolates the triceps.
steps: Stand or sit holding one dumbbell with both hands overhead, your palms under the top end.
Keep your upper arms close to your head with your elbows pointing forward.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Extend your arms to press it back up.
tips: Keep your core braced so your back does not arch.
Use a lighter weight than you think you need.
commonMistakes: Elbows flaring out to the sides.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: An explosive hip hinge that builds the glutes and hamstrings and raises your heart rate.
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and a kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
Hinge at your hips, grip the handle with both hands and hike the bell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to stand tall, letting the bell float up to chest height.
Let the bell fall and hinge your hips back as it swings between your legs.
Repeat in a smooth rhythm.
tips: The power comes from your hips, not your arms.
Start with a light kettlebell to learn the hinge.
commonMistakes: Lifting the bell with your arms.

name: Stationary Bike
description: Low-impact cycling for cardio fitness that is easy on the joints.
steps: Set the seat to hip height so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Pedal at an easy resistance for 3 to 5 minutes to warm up.
Raise the resistance to a pace where you breathe hard but can still speak in short sentences.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and a light grip on the handlebars.
Finish with 3 to 5 minutes of easy pedalling.
tips: Spin at a steady, smooth cadence rather than grinding at high resistance.
commonMistakes: Seat set too low or too high.
Rocking the hips from side to side.

name: Rowing Machine
description: A full-body cardio machine that works the legs, back and arms together.
steps: Sit on the seat, strap your feet in and grip the handle with straight arms and your shins vertical.
Drive through your legs first.
Lean back slightly, then pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Reverse the order to return: arms out, lean forward, then bend your knees to slide back.
Keep a steady rhythm.
tips: Think legs, then body, then arms on the way back, and the reverse on the way in.
Do not rush the recovery.

name: Incline Walk
description: A brisk walk on an inclined treadmill that burns calories with little impact.
steps: Clip the safety key to your clothing and start the belt at a slow walk.
Raise the speed to a brisk walk, around 5 to 6 kilometers per hour.
Increase the incline to about 8 to 12 percent.
Walk tall with relaxed arms swinging, without holding the handrails.
Lower the incline and slow down for the last few minutes to cool down.
tips: Start with a lower incline and build up over a few sessions.
commonMistakes: Setting the incline too steep to keep good form.
